Judgment

1 By this judgment I will dispose of appeal u/sec.374 Cr.PC. filed on behalf of Sh. Inderdeo Tripathi and M/s Som Products against the judgment dated 28.01.2016 and order on sentence dated 12.02.2016 passed by Ms. Priya Mahendra, then Ld. ACMM-II, Patiala House Court, New Delhi.
Inderdeo Tripathi & Ors. Vs. State 2

The brief facts of the case as per record and from trial court record are that accused is running an establishment namely M/s Som Products at C-123,
Naraina Industrial Area, New Delhi- 110028.

On 08.04.2008 at about 11.45 a.m. Food Inspector Sh.
Prem Chand Tiwari visited the said place and purchased 9 sealed poly packets of "Flavoured Pan Masala" each containing 60 pouches of two grams (ready for sale) from accused/appellant.
FI was accompanied with SDM/LHA Sh. S. M. Bhardwaj.
The said Pan Masala was purchased for the purposes of analysis under PFA Act.
The same sample was divided into three parts, packed as per Rules of PFA.
Panchanama was prepared.
One sample was sent for analysis to Public Analyst.
As per the report of Analyst, sample did not confirm to the standard because "The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Rule-32(i).
However Paan Masala conforms to the standard."
3 As the sample was failed, prosecution was launched by Food Inspector by filing complaint dated 02.09.2008 with the court.
Accused was summoned.

He has not exercised his right u/sec.13(2) PFA Asj vs The State (Da) on 17 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155939014/
1 Act and get the sample analyzed by CFL.
4 Charge was framed against accused u/sec.2(ix) (k) read with sec.7 of PFA Act, 1954 punishable u/sec.16(1a) of PFA Act.
5 A f t e r t r i a l , v i d e j u d g m e n t d a t e d 2 8 .
0 1 . 2 0 1 6 a p p e l l a n t  Inderdeo Tripathi & Ors.
Vs. State

no . 1 was convicted for offence u/sec.16(1a) of PFA Act and vide order on sentence dated 12.02.2016 was directed to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 6 months and fine of Rs.25,000/- and in default of payment of fine SI of 15 days.
The appellant no. 2/company i.e. M/s Som Products was directed to pay fine of Rs.50,000/-.

6 In this appeal, the accused has assailed the judgment on the following grounds:-
(i) There is no requirement of writing "best before" on the outer package.
( ii) The outer package was not required to be sold directly to the consumer.
7 No reply was filed by respondent/state and the matter was argued orally.
8 I have gone through the record, Trial Court record and have heard the submissions of Ld. counsel for appellant and Ld. SPP for State.
9 It is argued by counsel for appellant that there is no requirement of writing "best before" on the outer package.
It is further argued that there is no requirement for writing the same on the outer package as the outer package is not to be sold to the consumer directly.
As far as these argument are concerned, the same argument was raised before the Ld. Trial Court.
The same  Inderdeo Tripathi & Ors. Vs. State were dealt by the trial court from para 13 to 20 of the judgment.

As far as opinion/finding of the trial court regarding this argument is concerned, the thrust of the finding is that, on the package, it was not written that the package is intended not to be sold to single consumer.
In the absence of such declaration, the outer package cannot be considered as "wholesale package" in terms of Rule 32 (i) explanation (VI) of PFA Rules.
10 As far as the law discussed in various judgments by Hon. High Court, the same appears to be correct and valid but as per the facts mentioned in those judgments.
11 However, as far as the present case in hand is concerned, the facts are to be analyzed as per record.

From the perusal of the report of Public Analyst dated 29.04.2008 proved as Ex.PW1/F (in the trial court), the PA reported as under:-
"The condition of seals on the container and the outer covering on receipt was as follows:-
Asj vs The State (Da) on 17 October, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155939014/
2
Seals were intact & identical to the specimen impression of the seal received from Food Inspector.
I found the sample to be Pan Masala falling under item no. A.30 of Appendix B of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rule, 1955/Proprietary food.

The Sample was in a condition fir for analysis and has been analyzed on starting of analysis- 10/4/2008 and completion of analysis-16.06.2008 and the result of its analysis are given below/was not in a condition fit for analysis for the reason given below:- Analysis Report:-
 Inderdeo Tripathi & Ors. Vs. State  (i) Sample Description:-
Dilbagh
Flavoured
Pan Masala sample in original sealed small pouches contained inside another original packet.
(ii) Physical Appearance:- Brown coloured sample of Pan Masala.
(iii) Label:- Without declaration of Best Before."

So, according to this PA report it is admitted case of both the parties before me that there was an outer package "original packet" and after opening the same PA found small sealed pouches of Pan Masala inside the said "original packet."
12 Ld.

Trial court had giving finding that this "original packet" cannot be termed as "wholesale package" in terms of Sec.32(i) explanation (VI) PFA Rules, 1955 as it does not contain any stipulation/marking stating that it is not intended for sale directly to the consumer.
13 As far as this reasoning of the trial court is concerned, the same appears to be erroneous.
The PFA Act/rules are silent regarding the disclosure of information on the outer package/wholesale package i.e. it should show in writing that it is wholesale package.
14 The nature of the package itself shows that it is the inner product i.e. small original sealed pouches containing the Pan Masala which are to be sold and not the outer package.
Inderdeo Tripathi & Ors. Vs. State 15

So, accordingly, it can be safely said that the outer package which was termed as "original packet" by the PA in itself report dated 29.04.2008 is in fact is "wholesale package" as mentioned in Rule 32 (i) explanation (VI) of PFA Act, and thus exempted for writing "Best Before".
16
In these circumstances, the judgment of trial court is set aside.
17 Accused Inderdeo Tripathi and M/s Som Products are acquitted of the charges u/sec.16(1a) read with sec.7 of PFA Act.
18 Bail Bond u/sec.437A Cr.P.C. already furnished.
Accepted for six months.
